title: Hybrid INT8/FP8 quantization pipeline: calibration orchestration and runtime kernel compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a production-grade orchestration pipeline for hybrid INT8/FP8 quantization (SmoothQuant-style activation-aware transforms) that produces deployable quantization profiles and corresponding runtime kernel compatibility mappings. Goals: (1) produce repeatable calibration artifacts (per-layer/per-channel scale maps, activation compensation metadata) from a golden calibration corpus; (2) validate accuracy against our evaluation harness with regression thresholds and automatic gating; (3) generate runtime-side kernel selection metadata and fallback strategies (float fallback, variant kernels) to ensure safe rollouts; (4) integrate pipeline outputs into CI and the model catalog so Dedicated/Private deployments can pin profiles. Non-goals: inventing new quant algorithms — we use established SmoothQuant-style transforms and focus on orchestration, validation, and runtime compatibility.

Acceptance criteria: - Calibration pipeline accepts a model + corpus and emits a profile bundle (quant tables, compensation vectors, profile version) and a compatibility matrix linking model ops to quantized kernel variants. - End-to-end accuracy delta <= 0.8% on representative QA/LM tasks vs FP32 for target families; guardrail thresholds configurable per model family. - P95 token-latency increase <= 5% on typical KV-cache-heavy workloads when using quantized kernels vs baseline runtime. - CI gate that blocks merge on accuracy regressions with reproducible diff artifacts and golden-corpus traces. - Fallback semantics defined: runtime automatically routes to float kernels for layers marked 'unsafe' and to alternate quant kernels when unsupported hardware detected.

Approach: - Calibration orchestrator CLI/service (calib-orch) will run calibration sweeps (per-layer, per-channel, and prefix-balanced modes) across a sampled corpus. - Produce canonical artifact: profile.json (flat mapping), interpretable provenance metadata, and a small binary artifact (profile.bin) consumable by the serving runtime. - Validation harness runs accuracy evaluations (QA F1, LM next-token perplexity, token-level cross-entropy) and produces a regression report with examples and rolling averages. - Kernel compatibility generator maps ops to runtime kernel implementations (microkernel families for A100/H100/ARM GPUs, quantized path labels, and fallback rules). - Runtime: extend kernel selector to read profile bundle and compatibility matrix; add canary rollout flag to force flow to quantized kernels in prod lanes. - Observability: add telemetry events for "calib_profile_applied", "quant_kernel_fallback", and per-route token-cost delta.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: calibration overfits golden corpus -> mitigation: holdout eval set + diversity heuristics and randomization seeds. - Risk: perf regression on KV-cache heavy long-context workloads -> mitigation: early perf microbenchmarks in CI and staged canary on Dedicated pools. - Risk: unsupported operator variants on some GPUs -> mitigation: mark operator mapping as 'requires-hotpatch' and provide runtime float fallback.

Rollout Plan: design doc -> prototype PR -> internal perf/accuracy tuning (bench cluster) -> gated canary on non-critical tenant -> Dedicated pilot customers -> general availability in runtime-1.20. Monitoring and automatic rollback hooks included.
